summary: Defines a set of additional values for the NAS-Port-Type RADIUS attribute. It is an informational memo.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo adds five values to the RADIUS NAS-Port-Type attribute. Each value names a different way of carrying PPP traffic over ATM, Ethernet, or VLANs.

questions: what does pppoa mean in rfc 4603
subtitle: Five additional RADIUS NAS-Port-Type values for PPP connection types.

tldr.problem: The NAS-Port-Type RADIUS attribute needed values for several PPP connection types.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines values 30 through 34 for PPPoA and four PPP over Ethernet variants.
tldr.outcome: IANA registered the requested values; the IESG note cautions that this RFC was not reviewed as an Internet Standard candidate.

today: RFC 4603 is an Informational memo that records IANA registration of NAS-Port-Type values 30 through 34. Its IESG note cautions that the RFC is not a candidate for an Internet Standard.

sections.title: The NAS-Port-Type Attribute
sections.content:
The RFC defines new values for the NAS-Port-Type attribute described in RFC 2865. The attribute values identify the type of access connection represented in RADIUS.

The IESG note says this RFC is not a candidate for any level of Internet Standard and cautions readers to assess its suitability for implementation and deployment.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo adds labels for connection types in a RADIUS attribute. Its IESG note warns that publication does not amount to a standards endorsement.

sections.title: The Five New Values
sections.content:
The assigned values are 30 for PPPoA, 31 for PPPoEoA, 32 for PPPoEoE, 33 for PPPoEoVLAN, and 34 for PPPoEoQinQ. The names describe PPP carried over ATM, Ethernet, VLAN, or QinQ arrangements.

The RFC says these values had already been implemented by at least one vendor before IANA assigned them.
sections.plainLanguage: Each new number identifies a PPP connection arrangement. The memo says a vendor had already implemented the values before registration.

sections.title: IANA Registration and Security
sections.content:
The document serves as a request for IANA to allocate the listed values in the appropriate RADIUS registry, under the policy in RFC 3575. The text states that IANA registered the numbers.

The security section says the specification neither adds to nor detracts from RADIUS security.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA added the five values to the RADIUS registry. The RFC says the change does not affect RADIUS security.
